content: The Epworth Sleepiness Scale is a questionnaire designed to assess the level of daytime sleepiness in individuals. It is often used as a diagnostic tool to help identify potential sleep disorders. The questionnaire asks individuals to evaluate how likely they are to doze off or fall asleep in various situations, as opposed to simply feeling tired. This assessment is based on their typical lifestyle and recent experiences. Even if the individual has not encountered some of the listed situations recently, they are encouraged to estimate how those scenarios might have affected them. The scoring system is as follows: 0 indicates no chance of dozing. 1 indicates a slight chance of dozing. 2 indicates a moderate chance of dozing. 3 indicates a high chance of dozing. To determine the level of sleepiness, the individual adds up their scores across all situations: A total score between 1 and 6 suggests that the individual is likely getting sufficient sleep. A score of 7 or 8 is considered average. A score of 9 or higher indicates the need to consult a sleep specialist promptly. The Epworth Sleepiness Scale was created by Dr. Murray Johns at the Epworth Hospital in Melbourne, Australia. Additional resources related to the Epworth Sleepiness Scale can be found online, including: A page by Dr. William Dement of Stanford University, cited as (Dement 2000). SleepQuest, a commercial site associated with Dr. Dement. DrugDigest.org, cited as (DrugDigest 2005). SleepEducation.com.
